title: Canada Commits $24.5M to Plant 5 Million Trees Across Saskatchewan
detail: On July 7, 2026, Canada's federal government announced $24.5 million in funding for eight tree-planting projects across Saskatchewan under the 2 Billion Trees program, supporting the planting of more than 5 million trees. The largest single allocation — nearly $7.9 million — goes to the Kitsaki Management Limited Partnership (Lac La Ronge Indian Band) for boreal forest regeneration on wildfire-affected land, targeting 3.5–4 million trees. Other funded projects include the Métis Nation–Saskatchewan Home and Future Forest Project ($6.96M for 618,000 trees) and the Saskatchewan Woodland Caribou Habitat Restoration project ($6.35M to restore 350 hectares and plant 417,000 trees). The projects aim to restore wildfire-affected habitat, protect species at risk, and advance Indigenous-led reforestation, and were approved prior to the federal government's Budget 2025 announcement to wind down the 2 Billion Trees program.

media.caption: Federal officials announce $24.5M in tree-planting funding for Saskatchewan, July 2026

title: Indonesia Launches 2026–2028 Mangrove Promotion Strategy, Freeport Pledges 12,000 Hectares
detail: On July 7, 2026, Indonesia's Ministry of Environment launched a national mangrove promotion strategy for 2026–2028, framing environmental 'carrying capacity' as the foundation for future development policy. Environment Minister Mohammad Jumhur Hidayat announced the strategy in Sumbawa, West Nusa Tenggara (NTB), calling for collective 'ecological repentance' from government, corporations, and communities alike. Roughly 700,000 hectares — about 30% of Indonesia's 3.4 million hectares of mangroves — are degraded from land conversion and industrial activity. As an early corporate benchmark, mining giant Freeport Indonesia pledged to rehabilitate approximately 12,000 hectares nationwide (10,000 ha in Papua, 2,000 ha across other coastlines) and reported completing 484 hectares of mangrove rehabilitation in NTB — its largest mangrove program outside Papua — using roughly 1.5 million Rhizophora seedlings planted with 1,500 local residents.

media.caption: Indonesia's Environment Minister launches the 2026–2028 mangrove promotion strategy in Sumbawa, NTB
